speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of the lungs, flattened diaphragms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the X-ray results; the hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms are significant findings. Does your cough worsen at night or with exertion, and have you noticed any wheezing or chest tightness? Additionally, do you smoke or have a history of allergies or asthma?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, my cough definitely gets worse at night and I feel quite short of breath when I try to exercise. I do smoke about a pack a day and have had seasonal allergies for years, but I haven't felt any chest tightness or heard myself wheezing. However, a senior cardiologist from the referring clinic has already confirmed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. No further workup is needed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have a confirmed diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, but the hyperinflated lungs and worsening cough at night strongly suggest concurrent chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and possible cor pulmonale. Given your smoking history and the X-ray findings, do you have any swelling in your legs or ankles, or have you noticed a recent increase in your daily weight?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) with concomitant COPD
